questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD ability to implement per-namespace GitOps, use InitContainers, ConfigMaps, PVCs, and NetworkPolicy; validates YAML tooling, apply flow, and status reporting.

## Key Concepts
- Per-namespace GitOps design patterns
- InitContainer provisioning and tool installation
- YAML validation with kubeval and yamllint
- ConfigMap and Secret usage for configuration
- PVC-based log streaming and persistence
- Namespace-scoped NetworkPolicy for egress control
- Drift detection and status reporting via ConfigMap

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal skeleton for a per-namespace GitOps runner
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gitops-runner
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gitops-runner
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gitops-runner
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: git-clone
        image: alpine/git:latest
        env:
        - name: REPO_URL
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: gitops-config
              key: repo-url
        - name: TARGET_PATH
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: gitops-config
              key: target-path
        volumeMounts:
        - name: workspace
          mountPath: /workspace
        command:
        - /bin/sh
        - -c
        - |
          apk add --no-cache git yq
          git clone $(REPO_URL) /workspace/repo
          cd /workspace/repo
          yq eval '.spec.path = "$(TARGET_PATH)"' . > manifests.yaml
      containers:
      - name: validator
        image: kubeval/kubeval:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: workspace
          mountPath: /workspace
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
        command:
        - /bin/sh
        - -c
        - |
          kubeval /workspace/manifests.yaml > /logs/validation.log 2>&1
          yamllint -d relaxed /workspace/manifests.yaml >> /logs/validation.log 2>&1
          kubectl apply -f /workspace/manifests.yaml --namespace=$(NAMESPACE)
          kubectl get -f /workspace/manifests.yaml -o jsonpath='{.status}' > /gitops-status
      volumes:
      - name: workspace
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: gitops-logs
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a namespace-scoped automation that enforces resource policies, uses ConfigMaps for defaults, and reports via PVCs and status ConfigMaps. Requires practical use of CronJobs, InitContainers, and patching, plus RBAC and network controls.

## Key Concepts

- Namespace-scoped CronJob and per-namespace scope
- Deployments, resourceRequests, resourceLimits
- ConfigMap as defaults and heartbeat/status store
- InitContainer for kubectl/jq installation
- Patch operations to enforce defaults (idempotent)
- Logs via PVC and readiness/liveness probes
- Namespace NetworkPolicy limiting egress to API server

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: ns-resource-guard
spec:
  schedule: "*/5 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: ns-resource-guard-sa
          initContainers:
          - name: install-tools
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq && echo done"]
          containers:
          - name: guard
            image: bitnami/kubectl:1.28
            command: ["sh", "-c", "kubectl get deploy --all-namespaces -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.containers[]?.resources?.requests==null or .spec.template.spec.containers[]?.resources?.limits==null) | .metadata.namespace' | sort -u | while read ns; do kubectl -n $ns patch deploy --type=json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources","value": {"requests": {"cpu":"100m","memory":"128Mi"}, "limits": {"cpu":"200m","memory":"256Mi"}}}]' || true; done"]
          volumes:
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: logs-pvc
          - name: defaults
            configMap:
              name: resource-defaults
          tolerations:
          - operator: Exists
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you ensure patch idempotence and handle multi-container deployments?
- What RBAC would you restrict for the CronJob's service account?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to orchestrate time-based batch workloads, integrate ConfigMaps and Secrets with PVs, and enforce idempotence and rollback for Kubernetes workload automation.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob with Job template and parallelism
- ConfigMap mounted as /etc/reconcile
- PVC mounted at /data/reconcile
- Secret-provided DB credentials via env vars
- Resource requests/limits and graceful termination
- checksum/config annotation to trigger updates
- RBAC: RoleBinding for service account

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: reconcile-cron
  namespace: data-warehouse
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            checksum/config: "abcdef1234" # placeholder hash
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: reconcile-sa
          containers:
          - name: reconciler
            image: my-registry/reconcile:latest
            envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: db-creds
            volumeMounts:
            - name: reconcile-rules
              mountPath: /etc/reconcile
            - name: reconcile-output
              mountPath: /data/reconcile
            resources:
              requests:
                cpu: "200m"
                memory: "256Mi"
              limits:
                cpu: "500m"
                memory: "512Mi"
          volumes:
          - name: reconcile-rules
            configMap:
              name: reconcile-rules
          - name: reconcile-output
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: reconcile-pvc
          terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

```yaml
# RBAC skeleton (Role + RoleBinding)
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  namespace: data-warehouse
  name: reconcile-cron-role
rules:
- apiGroups: ["batch"]
  resources: ["jobs"]
  verbs: ["create", "get", "list", "watch"]
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: reconcile-cron-binding
  namespace: data-warehouse
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: reconcile-sa
  namespace: data-warehouse
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: reconcile-cron-role
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates comprehensive understanding of Kubernetes backup strategies, per-namespace automation patterns, and production-ready deployment practices. It tests the ability to coordinate multiple Kubernetes resources while maintaining proper isolation and observability.

## Key Concepts
- VolumeSnapshot API integration with VolumeSnapshotClass configuration
- Per-namespace CronJob deployment with appropriate RBAC boundaries
- ConfigMap-based state management for backup status tracking
- PVC-backed logging infrastructure with InitContainer tool deployment
- Namespace-scoped NetworkPolicy implementation for egress control
- Operational considerations including cadence optimization and retention policies

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: backup-scheduler
  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
spec:
  schedule: "0 0/12 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: install-tools
            image: busybox:1.35
            command: ['sh', '-c', 'apk add --no-cache velero jq']
          containers:
          - name: backup
            image: velero/velero:latest
            command: ['sh', '-c', 'velero snapshot create --from-pvc app-data && kubectl create configmap backup-status --from-literal=status=completed --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -']
            volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
            readinessProbe:
              exec:
                command: ['pgrep', 'velero']
              initialDelaySeconds: 10
            livenessProbe:
              exec:
                command: ['pgrep', 'velero']
              initialDelaySeconds: 30
          volumes:
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: backup-logs
```

## Trade-offs Discussion
**Frequency vs. Resource Consumption**: 12-hour intervals balance data protection requirements against cluster resource utilization and storage costs.

**Per-namespace vs. Cluster-wide**: Namespace-scoped deployment provides better isolation but increases operational complexity compared to a centralized backup controller.

**Storage Considerations**: VolumeSnapshot API offers efficient storage but requires compatible storage classes and may incur additional costs based on provider pricing models.

**Network Policy Impact**: Egress restrictions enhance security but may complicate troubleshooting and require careful endpoint whitelisting.

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: image-pull-policy-enforcer

spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: image-pull-policy-enforcer
  template:

      labels:
        app: image-pull-policy-enforcer

      initContainers:
      - name: install-kubectl

        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
      containers:
      - name: enforcer
        image: myorg/enforcer:latest
        envFrom:
        - configMapRef:

        - secretRef:
            name: enforcer-webhook-creds
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs

          httpGet:
            path: /health

          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10

          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20

      - name: logs

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD skills: CronJobs, Jobs, ConfigMaps, Secrets, PVCs, and RBAC in a single cohesive workflow. Emphasizes idempotence, cleanup, and rollback in a real maintenance task.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob and Job lifecycle
- ConfigMap and Secret integration
- PersistentVolumeClaim mounts
- ServiceAccount with RoleBinding
- ttlSecondsAfterFinished and history limits
- Observability: logs and data integrity

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: daily-archive
  namespace: data-archive
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: archive-sa
      ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          volumes:
            - name: data
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: data-pvc
            - name: archive
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: archive-pvc
          containers:
            - name: archiver
              image: myorg/archive-tool:latest
              imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
              envFrom:
                - configMapRef:
                    name: archive-config
                - secretRef:
                    name: archive-creds
              volumeMounts:
                - name: data
                  mountPath: /data
                - name: archive
                  mountPath: /archive
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "archive --older-than ${ARCHIVE_DAYS} --src /data --dst /archive"]
              resources:
                requests:
                  cpu: "100m"
                  memory: "128Mi"
                limits:
                  cpu: "500m"
                  memory: "512Mi"
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 1000
```

## Follow-up Questions

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests knowledge of namespace-scoped governance primitives (LimitRange, ResourceQuota) and how defaults affect scheduling, QoS, and multi-tenant fairness in CKAD.

## Key Concepts
- Namespace scoping
- LimitRange defaultRequests/defaultLimits
- ResourceQuota hard limits
- Pod scheduling under quotas
- Impact on autoscaling and experimentation

## Code Example
```yaml
# Namespace
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: test-ns
---
# LimitRange
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: default-limits
  namespace: test-ns
spec:
  limits:
  - default:
      cpu: 200m
      memory: 256Mi
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
    type: Container
---
# ResourceQuota
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: resource-quota
  namespace: test-ns
spec:
  hard:
    pods: "10"
    requests.cpu: "1"
    requests.memory: 1Gi
    limits.cpu: "2"
    limits.memory: 2Gi
---
# Deployment (inherits defaults)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: sample-app
  namespace: test-ns
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: sample-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: sample-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
```

## Trade-offs
**Advantages:**
- Prevents resource starvation across namespaces
- Enforces fair resource distribution
- Automatic defaults reduce configuration errors
- Provides cost control boundaries

**Considerations:**
- Too restrictive limits can hinder scaling
- Default limits may be overprovisioned for small workloads
- ResourceQuota refusals require manual quota increases
- May impact autoscaling behavior if quotas are too tight

**Best Practices:**
- Set conservative defaults but allow overrides
- Monitor quota utilization regularly
- Use separate quotas for production vs development
- Consider pod priority classes for critical workloads

## Trade-offs
- **Per-namespace vs. cluster-wide**: A per-namespace deployment provides isolation and TTL flexibility per namespace but increases resource overhead. A cluster-wide operator is more efficient but less flexible.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement a practical, namespace-scoped canary upgrade using standard CKAD tools: CronJob scheduling, patching Deployments, ConfigMaps/Secrets for config and credentials, and PVC-based logging. It also exercises InitContainers, probes, and network policy considerations in a real workflow.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scheduling and JobTemplate execution
- Patching Deployment images with kubectl set image or patch
- Reading image tag from ConfigMap and registry authentication via Secret
- Persisting status in a ConfigMap and logging to a PVC
- InitContainer to install tooling (kubectl, jq)
- Readiness/Liveness probes for the Job Pod
- Namespace NetworkPolicy restricting registry egress

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: canary-upgrade
spec:
  schedule: "*/10 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: canary-sa
          initContainers:
          - name: install-tools
            image: alpine:3.17
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq; true"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          containers:
          - name: upgrader
            image: bitnami/kubectl:latest
            command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "set -e; CANARY_TAG=$(kubectl get configmap canary-config -o jsonpath='{.data.tag}'); kubectl patch deployment my-app -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"my-app","image":"myrepo/my-app:${CANARY_TAG}"}]}}}}' --record; echo done; sleep 1"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          volumes:
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: logs-pvc
          imagePullSecrets:
          - name: registry-credentials
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to implement idempotent patches and roll back on failure?
- How to measure canary success (latency, error rate) before full rollout?
- How would this scale across many namespaces or deployments?

Why This Is Asked

Key Concepts

- PVC-mounted manifests and ConfigMap-driven batching
- Secret-based credentials and TLS rotation sidecar
- Readiness/Liveness probes and per-namespace NetworkPolicy
- Minimal YAML skeleton and trade-offs between latency and throughput

Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: image-scan-guardian
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: image-scan-guardian
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: image-scan-guardian
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: scanner
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do sleep 60; done"]
          volumeMounts:
            - mountPath: /images
              name: images
        - name: main
          image: busybox:1.36
          command: ["sh", "-c", "echo running; sleep 3600"]
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: image-config
      initContainers:
        - name: install-scanner
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache --update curl jq && echo scanner installed"]
      volumes:
        - name: images
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: images-pvc
      imagePullSecrets:
        - name: reg secret
```
